heroHeadline: IFT-12 at T-2 (NET May 19, 5:30 PM CDT) — Starship V3 Final Countdown Underway; Artemis II Crew Day 37 at JSC; Artemis III 460 km Earth-Orbit Profile Confirmed
heroSubtitle: May 17: SpaceX Starship IFT-12 (Booster 19 + Ship 39 — Starship V3 debut) entered T-2 day pre-launch operations at Orbital Launch Pad 2, Starbase, with all systems go and no technical or regulatory holds. NET window remains May 19 at 5:30 PM CDT (22:30 UTC), extending through May 21. IFT-12 is the first Starship flight to carry the pressurized docking port and propellant-transfer interface hardware mandated by NASA for Artemis III HLS qualification — a critical precursor milestone for Artemis IV's 2028 crewed lunar landing. NASA published the preliminary Artemis III mission profile on May 14: Orion will rendezvous and dock with the SpaceX Starship HLS pathfinder AND Blue Origin Blue Moon Mk2 at ~460 km LEO to test AxEMU spacesuits, lander life support, propulsion, and crew-interface procedures — targeting late 2027. Artemis II crew — Commander Reid Wiseman, Pilot Victor Glover, Mission Specialist Christina Koch, and Canadian Mission Specialist Jeremy Hansen (CSA) — are at Johnson Space Center on Day 37 post-splashdown (Orion splashed down April 10), conducting post-flight debriefs and physiological recovery. At KSC's Multi-Payload Processing Facility, heat shield visual inspection of the Artemis II Orion crew module continues; formal Marshall X-ray scans and Avcoat sample extractions remain on track for summer 2026. Artemis III SLS core stage stacking advances in VAB High Bay 2. Artemis Accords at 67 nations.
